dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation

evidence.note: Systematically characterized both pairs: read graph headers (|V|,|E|), sampled node names, computed degree distributions and connected components, and ran baseline heuristics (degree-sort, BFS order) with local S3 measurement — a quantified baseline characterization.

Recognized node IDs as likely Entrez Gene IDs and researched biological orthology (NCBI HomoloGene) as a candidate signal, then quantified its S3 (~0.013) and rejected it, showing method-fit evaluation.

Identified SANA as an established published aligner purpose-built for S3 optimization and pursued it; noticed EC-vs-S3 objective levers. Selected a known-reasonable approach with stated rationale, but did not comparatively evaluate multiple published methods (IsoRank/MAGNA) against instance sizes.

Recognized reference alignment gives NC=1.0 via copy (name/reference lever for NC) but only checked its S3 at step 87, discovering it failed the 0.55 threshold — a late-caught orientation gap on the yeast dual-constraint deliverable.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent systematically characterized each pair (sizes, degrees, components, node-naming), quantified baseline scores, researched concrete methods (orthology, SANA), and noticed the task-specific levers (reference-seeding for NC vs topology for S3, per-deliverable constraints), matching anchor 8. It falls short of 10 because it converged on a single published tool rather than comparatively evaluating several against instance sizes/runtime, and did not verify the yeast copy's S3 baseline up front (discovered only at step 87).

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones

evidence.note: Built test_align.py to compute S3/Ea/E2 on several baseline alignments before writing any optimizer — scorer-first sequencing, and separates parsing/scoring/alignment-generation stages.

Treated yeast as 'done' by copying the perfect alignment at step 3 and only verified its S3 at step 87, discovering it fails the 0.55 threshold — the yeast done-check milestone was deferred to the very end, a decomposition lapse.
Each optimization pass reports measured S3 vs the 0.32 target and gates keep/restore of 'best' files on the measured score — numeric done-criteria per iteration.

After the yeast S3 gap surfaced, added a distinct NC-vs-S3 hybridization sub-goal with its own numeric targets (force ~312 nodes to reference targets while keeping S3>=0.55) — evidence of per-deliverable threshold tracking, but reactive rather than planned.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds level 5: it separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, builds the scorer before optimizing against it, and gates each optimization iteration on measured S3 vs the 0.32/0.55/0.30 thresholds with 'best' backups. It falls short of level 8 because the yeast deliverable's threshold milestone was never verified until the final steps (assuming copy=done), effort was mis-budgeted heavily toward DM-HS, and milestones emerged reactively rather than as an explicit ordered hierarchy — placing it in the 6-7 band, at 6 given the significant yeast gating oversight.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics

evidence.note: Builds /app/test_align.py to compute S3/Ea/E2 locally on baseline heuristics before trusting any alignment — metric implementation established early.

Every candidate scored with exact S3 reporting Ea and E2_aligned separately (e.g. 'S3≈0.234235 (Ea=10620, E2=21206)'); score used as the accept/reject and stopping objective ('keep if better, restore best if worse').

Trusted Python scorer detects that exact_replace.cpp accepted moves on incorrect E2 deltas and overwrote the best with a worse alignment; agent recovers from backup — scorer guards against edge-set delta bugs in its own optimizers.
Validates output format ('well-formed'), checks full coverage (wc -l), and scores the reference alignment getting NC=1.0 + sensible S3≈0.248 — sanity-checks the metric implementation.
SANA reports S3≈0.557 for yeast; agent independently recomputes exact S3≈0.557 AND NC≈0.169, discovering NC fails — treats reported/passing score as necessary-but-scrutinized, not final.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent implemented faithful S3 and NC scorers, ran them on every alignment (tracking Ea and E2_aligned distinctly), verified injectivity/coverage/format, and sanity-checked by scoring the reference (NC=1.0), satisfying all anchor-8 criteria. It exceeds 8 with tight-feedback-loop behaviors: its trusted scorer caught an edge-set delta bug in its own C++ optimizer (step 53) and independently re-verified SANA's reported score to expose an NC failure (step 88). It stops short of a pure 10 only because there is no explicit edge-case unit-testing of the scorer's denominator, so I place it at 9.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization

evidence.note: Early continuous score reporting: greedy S3~0.12, replacement hill-climber to 0.216, swap improver 0.220 — establishes running best-so-far from the start.
Recognizes 'strong one-node local optimum' at 0.234235, backs up best (DM-HS.best234), and reasons about escaping the basin — plateau detection plus best-preservation.
Systematic mixed-weight sweep with per-step best backups (best240/243/246/247/248/249) and restore-if-worse discipline; tracks the S3 trend across weights and notes SANA runs 'plateaued'.
Switches to yeast, tracks BOTH S3 (0.557) and NC (0.169) against their thresholds, quantifies exactly how many nodes must be corrected (~714) to reach NC>=0.30.
Detects a buggy improver overwrote DM-HS.align with a worse (0.224) result and recovers from sana_seed backup — active regression detection.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintains an accurate, continuously-updated picture of S3 (and later NC) versus thresholds across ~90 steps, logs the full score progression, preserves best-so-far via explicit backup files, restores when variants regress, and recognizes local optima and SANA plateaus rather than looping blindly. This matches the level-8 anchor fully and most of level-10 (disciplined trajectory monitoring, distinguishes converging-slowly from stuck, preserves the best while exploring); it falls just short of a perfect 10 only because it never definitively concluded the DM-HS approach was exhausted, continuing nearby-weight variants with shrinking marginal gains until the trajectory ended.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met

evidence.note: Diagnosed that simple topology failed, tried external orthology (HomoloGene) as a different signal; got S3≈0.013 and abandoned it, then diagnosed random annealing as ineffective and pivoted to greedy construction.
Explicitly reasoned 'at current Ea even perfect E2 wouldn't reach 0.32; need to increase Ea', pivoting from replacement to swap-based search and then to downloading an established aligner (SANA).

Recognized the hot-temperature SANA run was collapsing the score (~0.09) and repeatedly tried to abort it, protecting the accumulated best (backed up as best234) rather than letting a bad run overwrite gains.

Formed the hypothesis that EC-weighted SANA reaches higher-Ea basins, then S3 improvers cut E2; ran a deliberate sweep of mixed EC/S3 weights, each followed by local improvers, keeping only improvements — though this later became somewhat repetitive grinding still short of 0.32.

For yeast, diagnosed the NC-vs-S3 tradeoff (perfect seed NC=1/S3=0.248 vs SANA S3=0.557/NC=0.169) and pivoted to a reference-seeded hybridizer to satisfy both constraints, iterating from a slow Python version to a faster C++ one.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly forms hypotheses about why a metric lags (Ea too low for S3; NC vs S3 tradeoff for yeast), tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals (orthology, topology/SANA, reference-seeding, hybridization) tuned to the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly while preserving accumulated gains via systematic backups — matching the level-10 description of fluid, evidence-driven course-correction. It falls just short of a perfect 10 because the DM-HS mixed-weight sweep became a somewhat repetitive parameter grind that never escaped its plateau, so I place it at 9.

rubric.task_read: An open-ended global network-alignment optimization task: produce two injective node mappings between PPI networks that clear specified S3 (topological) and NC (node-correctness) thresholds. The horizon is long and the difficulty is real — hitting the numeric targets likely requires researching/implementing a nontrivial alignment algorithm (e.g., seed-and-extend, IsoRank/SANA/MAGNA-style), plus building the S3/NC metrics locally since the metrics are fully specified but the grader is hidden. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in research, self-verification, and iterative optimization; the two deliverables have different constraints (one needs NC against a provided reference), so approaches may diverge.

dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation
dimensions.description: Inspecting the graph files/sizes and the reference alignment, and researching/selecting a suitable network-alignment approach before committing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: S3/NC thresholds are hard to hit with a naive mapping; the space of alignment algorithms is well-studied, and the provided reference alignment plus node-name overlap are exploitable signals. Acting blind almost guarantees thrash.

anchors.0: Starts writing a mapping with no look at graph sizes, file format, or the reference alignment; no consideration of what algorithm could work.
anchors.3: Skims one file and picks an arbitrary heuristic (e.g., degree-sort or random injective map) without weighing whether it can clear the thresholds.
anchors.5: Reads both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspects the reference alignment, and picks a known-reasonable approach (seed-and-extend, IsoRank, or an existing tool) with a stated rationale.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes each pair (|V|,|E|, degree distribution, shared node names), researches concrete alignment methods and their fit to S3 vs NC, and notices task-specific levers (name-overlap for NC, topology for S3; differing constraints per deliverable) that shape the plan.
anchors.10: Deep, sustained orientation: quantifies what score a baseline achieves, identifies the exact structural signal each threshold rewards, evaluates multiple published methods against the concrete instance sizes/runtime, and derives a targeted strategy per deliverable grounded in that analysis.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered sub-goals (parse → metric implementation → baseline alignment → optimization) each with a concrete done-check tied to the score thresholds.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Two deliverables with distinct constraints and a multi-stage pipeline mean undifferentiated 'just write the file' effort will strand the agent without knowing whether it's close.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no separable stages, no per-deliverable structure.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; treats both alignments as one blob and has no notion of intermediate checkpoints.
anchors.5: Separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, and tracks the two deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (parser verified → S3/NC computable → baseline score measured → optimize to threshold) each with a numeric done-criterion, sequenced sensibly (e.g., build the scorer before optimizing against it).
anchors.10: A crisp milestone hierarchy that also budgets effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (the NC-constrained yeast task vs the S3-only fly task), with fallback branches per milestone and clear gating on measured scores before advancing.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics
dimensions.description: Building/using a correct local implementation of S3 and NC (and injectivity/format checks) to measure alignments before trusting them.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader is hidden but the metrics are fully specified. An agent that cannot compute its own S3/NC is optimizing blind and cannot know if it passed; a subtly wrong scorer is worse than none.

anchors.0: Never computes S3 or NC; submits alignments hoping they pass.
anchors.3: Eyeballs coverage or computes a rough proxy, but no faithful S3/NC implementation; no format/injectivity validation.
anchors.5: Implements S3 and NC per the spec and runs them on its alignments, plus checks injectivity, full coverage of V1, and exact node-name/format matching.
anchors.8: Faithful metric implementation that it sanity-checks (e.g., scores the reference alignment to confirm NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3, tests edge cases like the E2_aligned denominator), and uses the score as the optimization objective/stopping test.
anchors.10: Rigorously validated scorer used as a tight feedback loop: cross-checks the S3 formula against the reference, guards against off-by-one/edge-set-double-counting bugs, verifies format matches the exact spec, and treats a passing local score as necessary-but-scrutinized rather than final.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across iterations and detecting stalled or plateaued optimization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Optimization can plateau below threshold; without tracking best-so-far scores the agent won't know if it's converging, stuck, or regressing across a long run.

anchors.0: No awareness of current scores or distance to thresholds; can't say whether it's improving.
anchors.3: Occasionally prints a number but no continuity — no sense of best-so-far or trend.
anchors.5: Tracks current S3/NC against each threshold and knows which deliverables still fall short.
anchors.8: Maintains best-so-far per deliverable across iterations, recognizes plateaus/regressions, and decides when an approach has stopped yielding gains rather than looping indefinitely.
anchors.10: Disciplined trajectory monitoring: logs score progression, distinguishes 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', avoids re-running variants that already failed, and preserves the best alignment while exploring — never loses the plot over a long optimization horizon.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met
dimensions.description: Changing algorithm, parameters, or signal (topology vs name-overlap vs reference-seeding) when the current approach plateaus below target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first-choice method may not reach S3≥0.55/NC≥0.30; success often depends on switching or combining strategies rather than grinding the same one.

anchors.0: Keeps the same failing approach (or ships a below-threshold file) despite no progress.
anchors.3: Minor tweaks only (reruns with a different seed) without diagnosing why it fell short.
anchors.5: When stuck, tries a materially different tactic (new algorithm, added seeding, tuned objective) prompted by the observed shortfall.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the cause of the shortfall (e.g., NC low → exploit name-overlap/reference seeding; S3 low → local topological search) and pivots deliberately, keeping what worked.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven course-correction: forms hypotheses about why a metric lags, tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals for the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly without discarding accumulated gains.
